name: event-sourcing
context: Systems requiring complete audit trails, temporal queries, and event replay capabilities. The event log serves as the source of truth rather than current state.
benefits: Complete audit trail: Every state change is captured as an immutable event
Temporal queries: Reconstruct state at any point in time
Event replay: Rebuild projections, fix bugs by replaying corrected events
Decoupled business logic: Events are simple facts, business rules in aggregates
Easy integration: Other services subscribe to event streams
Parallel processing: Multiple consumers can process events independently
Future-proof data: Events can be reprocessed into new read models
Debugging and traceability: Complete history aids forensic analysis
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency: Projections are updated asynchronously
Learning curve: Different mental model than CRUD requires team training
Query complexity: Reconstructing state requires event replay or projections
Event schema evolution: Upcasting requires careful versioning strategy
Large event streams: Snapshots needed to optimize rehydration
Operational complexity: Additional moving parts (event store, projectors, checkpoints)
use_cases: Audit trail is a regulatory or business requirement
Temporal queries needed (state at point in time)
Complex domain with many state transitions
Multiple read models needed from same event stream
Long-running business processes with compensating actions
avoid_when: Simple CRUD with no audit needs
Data volume too high for event storage costs
Team unfamiliar with event sourcing concepts
Strongly consistent reads immediately after writes required
Storage costs prohibitive for long-term event retention
component_types: Event Store: Append-only database of all domain events. Provides API for appending events and retrieving event streams by aggregate ID
Aggregate: Domain object that processes commands and emits events. State is reconstructed by replaying events
Command: Intent to change state, validated by aggregate before event emission
Event (Domain Event): Immutable record of something that happened (e.g., OrderPlaced, PaymentReceived)
Snapshot Store: Periodically saves aggregate state to avoid replaying all events from origin
Projection (Read Model): Derives viewable state from events. Multiple projections can coexist from same event stream
Upcaster: Converts old event versions to new schema during replay
anti_patterns: Mutable events: Modifying events after creation breaks immutability
State-focused events: Events capturing result rather than intent
Synchronous projections: Blocking writes for projection updates
In-place schema migration: Rewriting historical events
Missing idempotency: Projections that fail on duplicate events
Large aggregates: Storing too many events in single stream
No snapshot strategy: Replaying entire event history repeatedly
design_principles: Immutability: Events are never modified after creation; only new events can compensate for old ones
Intent over State: Events should capture business intent (what happened) not just resulting state
Aggregate Consistency: Aggregates enforce business invariants; events are the result of state transitions
Append-Only Storage: Event store never updates or deletes; enables replay and audit
Asynchronous Projections: Read models are built asynchronously to decouple read and write workloads
Schema Evolution: Event schemas evolve through upcasters, never by rewriting historical events
best_practices: Treat the event store as one big audit log: Never change or reorder events
Be explicit about information in events: Include full context needed at replay time
Use unique event identifiers: Associate projections with latest event processed
Default to asynchronous projections: Decouple read and write sides
Test projectors as units: Events in, query results out
Make rebuilding projections fast: Use aggressive caching, batch processing, NoSQL
Handle eventual consistency explicitly: Design UIs to handle stale data
Encrypt events at rest and in transit: Events contain sensitive business data
